<u>Summary</u>. The estimate of fuel economy loss due to the increased road loads range from 6.2 percent for GM (excluding increased NOx effects) to a maximum of 10 percent for Ford and AMC. Chrysler estimated an 8 percent loss.
Analysis. NHTSA recognizes that to present a proper basis for considering fuel economy standards the scenerio used must be consistent. If EPA's test procedures for MY 1979 are used as the basis for comparison, the benefits derived from the fuel economy standard will appear greater than those derived from using the MY 1976 test procedure. This apparent difference occurs because of the increased road loads specified for MY 1979.
An increase in test procedure road loads only reflects a gain or loss related to the test procedures. Changing the test procedure does not enhance or detract from the savings attributable to the operation of the vehicle.
